explanation: The OK hand sign (thumb and index finger forming a circle) is not read as 'okay' in Turkey. Multiple independent sources describe it as a serious, vulgar gesture that functions as a homophobic insult. This is understood across generations, though younger, urban Turks are somewhat more likely to also recognize the Western 'OK' meaning.
local_tip: Avoid the OK hand sign entirely in Turkey — nod, say 'tamam' (okay), or use a thumbs-up instead.

also_check.note: Considered a very offensive gesture, similar to an obscene insult.
Commonly used to mean 'okay' or 'good,' though some younger people use it ironically.
Widely used to mean 'OK' or 'money,' with no negative connotations.

sources.title: Not bad intentions, it's just etiquette in Turkey
